docs.title: GlobeTalk Documentation 🌍✉️
docs.text: Welcome to the official documentation for GlobeTalk, a virtual pen pal platform that connects people worldwide for text-based cultural exchange and global friendships. This site provides comprehensive guides for users and developers, covering features, APIs, UI, setup, and more.

docs.title: About GlobeTalk
docs.text:
GlobeTalk simulates the traditional pen pal experience through modern digital messaging, emphasizing curiosity, connection, and global diversity. Users can match with random pen pals, exchange delayed text messages, explore cultural profiles, and engage safely with moderated content.

Target Users:

  • Language learners
  • Cultural exchange enthusiasts
  • Students and educators

Travelers seeking global connections

docs.title: GlobeTalk Privacy Policy
docs.text:
Last updated: 19 October 2025

At GlobeTalk, your privacy and safety are our top priorities. Our goal is to create a safe, inclusive space where people around the world can connect through virtual pen pal conversations — without compromising their personal information.

docs.title: 1. Information We Collect
docs.text: We collect only the minimum information needed to make GlobeTalk work safely and meaningfully.

docs.title: a. Profile Information
docs.text:
When you create an account, you may provide: - Your preferred language - Age range - Region or approximate timezone (e.g., “South Africa (GMT+2)”) - Hobbies or interests - A short bio or cultural introduction

⚠️ We do not collect real names, phone numbers, email addresses, or precise location data.

docs.title: b. Matchmaking Data
docs.text:
To find compatible pen pals, we use: - Language and region preferences

No personally identifying information is shared during the matchmaking process.

docs.title: c. Messages
docs.text:
• Messages are text-only and stored securely.
  • Messages are private between matched users.
  • Moderators can review flagged messages only for rule violations.

docs.title: d. Moderation Data
docs.text:
If you report a user or message, GlobeTalk logs: - The report reason - The message or user ID involved - The moderation outcome (e.g., warning, suspension)

This helps maintain community safety.

docs.title: 2. How We Use Your Information
docs.text:
We use collected data to: - Match you with suitable pen pals - Deliver and store messages safely - Enforce safety and moderation rules - Improve the app’s performance and experience

We do not sell, rent, or share your data with third parties for marketing.

docs.title: 3. Data Sharing & Security
docs.text:
• All communications are encrypted during transmission.
  • User identities are hidden — we use unique IDs instead of real names or contact info.
  • Moderators can only view content necessary for rule enforcement.
  • Access to stored data is restricted to authorized personnel.

docs.title: 4. Anonymity & Safety
docs.text: GlobeTalk is designed for anonymous cultural exchange: - No sharing of personal contact details (emails, phone numbers, social media, etc.) - No media or file sharing — text-only messages - Users can block or report others at any time - Inappropriate content is reviewed and may lead to suspension or removal

docs.title: 5. Your Rights
docs.text: You can: - View or edit your profile details - Delete your account and data permanently - Request a copy of your message history - Report unsafe behavior or content

docs.title: 6. Data Retention
docs.text:
• Messages and match records are retained as long as the account is active.
  • Deleted accounts are permanently removed from our database within 30 days.
  • Moderation logs may be kept longer for safety and compliance reasons.

docs.title: 7. Children’s Privacy
docs.text: GlobeTalk is intended for users aged 18 and older. We do not knowingly collect information from minors under 16. If such data is discovered, it will be deleted immediately.

docs.title: 8. Updates to This Policy
docs.text: We may update this Privacy Policy to reflect new features or legal requirements. Any significant changes will be communicated through the app or our website.

docs.title: 9. Contact Us
docs.text: If you have questions, concerns, or privacy requests, please contact: 📧 globetalk92@gmail.com

docs.title: GlobeTalk Terms of Service
docs.text:
Last updated: 19 October 2025

Welcome to GlobeTalk, a virtual pen pal platform designed to connect people across the world through meaningful, anonymous cultural exchanges.

By creating an account or using GlobeTalk, you agree to these Terms of Service. Please read them carefully.

docs.title: 1. Purpose of GlobeTalk
docs.text:
GlobeTalk provides a safe, text-only environment where users can: - Match with pen pals based on language and region preferences - Exchange delayed text messages (simulating postal letters) - Share cultural insights, hobbies, and experiences respectfully

Our mission is to promote global curiosity, friendship, and cultural understanding.

docs.title: 2. Eligibility
docs.text:
• You must be 18 years or older to use GlobeTalk.
  • You may not use GlobeTalk if you have been previously banned.
  • By registering, you confirm that the information you provide (e.g., language, region, bio) is truthful and non-identifying.

docs.title: 3. User Responsibilities
docs.text:
You agree to: - Treat others with respect and kindness. - Keep all communication appropriate and culturally sensitive. - Never share personal contact information (e.g., phone numbers, email, social media). - Avoid using offensive, discriminatory, or explicit language. - Report any inappropriate or unsafe behavior through the in-app tools.

You are solely responsible for the messages and content you send through the platform.

docs.title: 4. Prohibited Conduct
docs.text:
You may not use GlobeTalk to: - Harass, threaten, or bully other users - Impersonate another person or share false information - Send explicit, violent, or hateful messages - Attempt to exchange external contact details or meet users outside the platform - Spam or advertise products or services - Circumvent moderation systems or exploit platform bugs

Violations of these rules may lead to temporary suspension or permanent account termination.

docs.title: 5. Anonymity and Safety
docs.text:
GlobeTalk is designed for anonymous cultural exchange: - Real names, photos, and personal contact details are not required or shared. - Messages are text-only (no media, images, or files). - Each user is identified only by a username and user ID. - You can block or report users at any time if you feel uncomfortable.

We encourage you to protect your privacy by avoiding self-identifying information.

docs.title: 6. Message Delays & Availability
docs.text:
• GlobeTalk messages may be delayed to simulate the experience of postal mail.
  • Delays can also occur due to moderation or server load.
  • We do not guarantee constant availability or delivery times, though we aim for reliability.

docs.title: 7. Moderation & Reporting
docs.text: To maintain community safety: - All reports are reviewed by moderators. - Repeated or severe violations may lead to a permanent ban. - Moderators may access reported messages only to review for violations. - We may remove content or accounts that violate these Terms or harm the community.

docs.title: 8. Account Termination
docs.text:
We reserve the right to suspend or delete accounts that: - Violate these Terms or our Privacy Policy - Are reported for harmful behavior - Are inactive for extended periods

You may delete your account at any time through the Settings page. Deleted data is permanently removed within 30 days.

  • You retain rights to the messages and bios you write but grant GlobeTalk a limited license to store and display them within the app.

docs.title: 10. Limitation of Liability
docs.text:
GlobeTalk is provided “as is” without warranties of any kind. We are not responsible for: - The content of user messages - Interactions between users outside the app - Technical interruptions or data loss

However, we take every reasonable measure to ensure a safe and reliable experience.

docs.title: Matchmaking API
docs.text: The Matchmaking API is responsible for pairing users as pen pals. It handles creating new matches, retrieving all matches for a user, updating match statuses (active, completed, blocked), and deleting matches. Whenever a user signs up or requests a new connection, this API determines which users are compatible and stores the match information in the database.

docs.title: Message API
docs.text: The Message API manages all user communications. It allows sending messages, retrieving messages in a match, and deleting messages. This ensures that users can exchange text messages in real-time or near real-time. Each message is linked to a match and contains information about the sender, recipient, content, and timestamp.

docs.title: Profile API
docs.text: The Profile API allows users to create, update, retrieve, or delete their cultural profiles. These profiles include information such as hobbies, languages, and other cultural notes that help improve matchmaking suggestions. This API ensures that users’ cultural data is stored securely and can be accessed when generating matches.

docs.title: Moderation API
docs.text: The Moderation API is used for reporting inappropriate behaviour and reviewing reported users. Users can file reports against other users, and administrators can retrieve, review, and take action based on these reports. This API helps maintain a safe and respectful environment within the app.

docs.title: 2. How to test each API using curl
Matchmaking API
docs.text:
Create a match: 

curl -X POST https://our-project-id/api/matches \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \
  -d '{
    "user1Id": "abc123",
    "user2Id": "def456",
    "status": "active"
  }'
Get all matches for a user: 
curl https://our-project-id/api/users/abc123/matches

docs.title: Message API
docs.text:
Send a message: 

curl -X POST https://our-project-id/api/matches/match789/messages \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \
  -d '{
    "senderId": "abc123",
    "recipientId": "def456",
    "text": "Hello!"
  }'
Get messages in a match: 
curl https://our-project-id/api/matches/match789/messages

docs.title: Profile API
docs.text:
Create/Update a cultural profile: 

curl -X POST https://our-project-id/api/culturalProfiles \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \
  -d '{
    "userId": "abc123",
    "languages": ["English", "Zulu"],
    "hobbies": ["reading", "cycling"],
    "culturalNotes": "Enjoys traditional music"
  }'
Get a cultural profile: 
curl https://our-project-id/api/culturalProfiles/abc123

docs.title: Moderation API
docs.text:
File a report: 

curl -X POST https://moderation-api.onrender.com/reports \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \
  -d '{
    "reportingUserId": "abc123",
    "reportedUserId": "def456",
    "reason": "Inappropriate behaviour"
  }'
Get all reports (admin): 
curl https://moderation-api.onrender.com/reports \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>"

docs.title: 3. Where was each API deployed?
docs.text:
• Matchmaking API: Publicly hosted (deployed on Render).
  • Message API: Publicly hosted (deployed on Render).
  • Profile API: Publicly hosted (deployed on Render).
  • Moderation API: Publicly hosted on Render (as verified).

docs.title: 4. How did we connect Render and GitHub for this API?
docs.text:
• The project code for each API was stored in a GitHub repository.
  • Render was connected to the GitHub repository so that every push to the main branch automatically triggered a deployment.
  • This allows the APIs to stay updated in real-time with the latest code from GitHub.

docs.title: 5. How to use each API as our group?
docs.text:
• Each group member can access the API using the base URL and endpoints.
  • Members need a Firebase authentication token to perform actions like sending messages, creating matches, or filing reports.
  • Team members can test APIs using curl commands or Postman.
  • Our group also has access credentials stored securely to manage and monitor the APIs.

docs.title: 6. How can other groups use our API?
docs.text:
• Other groups can access the APIs via the public endpoints provided (Render-hosted URLs).
  • They will need a valid Firebase token if authentication is required.
  • Example: They can test the Matchmaking API by sending requests to the same endpoints with their own data.
  • We can provide API documentation and example curl commands to help other groups integrate or test the APIs easily.

docs.title: 7. Where did our group currently store this API for access?
docs.text:
• All APIs are stored and deployed publicly on Render.
  • Source code for the APIs is in a GitHub repository that the group maintains.
  • Group members have access to both GitHub (for code) and Render (for deployed endpoints) for testing, debugging, and updating.

docs.title: COMMUNICATION TOOLS FOR TEAM AND CLIENT
1. Why we use WhatsApp for communication within our group ###
docs.text: Our group chose WhatsApp as our primary internal communication platform because it fits the way we already work together day-to-day. Almost every group member already has WhatsApp on their phone and uses it regularly, so there’s no need to learn a new platformer having to set it up. This means messages, calls, updates and quick clarifications can happen instantly without anyone needing to log in to a new tool. WhatsApp also has group chats, supports voice notes and file sharing, which allows us to handle everything from short check-ins to quick sharing of screenshots or documents. Notifications are lightweight and mobile-friendly, so even when we’re away from our computers we can stay connected and respond quickly. In short, WhatsApp lets us communicate in real time, informally but efficiently, with the least friction for the team.

docs.title: 2. Why we use Discord to communicate with the client
docs.text: For our interactions with the client we decided on Discord rather than WhatsApp. Discord gives us a slightly more structured environment and a clearer separation between our internal conversations and client facing communication. With Discord we can create a dedicated channel for us to communicate solely with a client when needed. It also provides better tools for hosting scheduled calls, screen sharing, and sharing larger files than WhatsApp does. This is especially useful when we’re walking the client through new features, gathering feedback, or running live demos. By keeping client communication on Discord, we maintain a professional yet accessible space for them to reach us, while protecting the privacy and informality of our internal WhatsApp chats.

docs.title: Branching Strategy
docs.text:
• Main Branch (main): Stable, production-ready code.
  • Testing Branch (testing): For integrating and validating features.
  • Feature Branches (feature/xyz): For new features or bug fixes.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Create a Feature Branch
  2. Name: feature/<short-description>
  3. Base: testing

  4. Example: git checkout -b feature/add-profile-endpoint testing

  5. Implement and Commit

  6. Use clear commit messages: type(scope): message

  7. Example: feat(api): add profile update endpoint

  8. Push to GitHub

  9. Push your feature branch: git push origin feature/add-profile-endpoint

  10. Create a Pull Request (PR)

  11. Base: testing
  12. Compare: Your feature branch

  13. Include a descriptive title and testing notes.

  14. Code Review

  15. At least one reviewer must approve.

  16. Reviewers check code quality, functionality, and no breaking changes.

  17. Testing

  18. Run tests locally: npm test
  19. Ensure 80% code coverage with Jest.

  20. CI pipeline runs unit and integration tests.

  21. Merging

  22. Merge feature to testing after approval and CI checks.
  23. Merge testing to main after validation.
  24. Delete merged feature branches.

docs.title: Database Components
docs.text: GlobeTalk uses Firebase Firestore for scalable, real-time data storage. Below are the main collections and their schemas.

docs.title: User Profiles
docs.text:
Stores user preferences and cultural information.

  • Collection: users
  • Document: <userId>
  • Fields: 
    {
  "region": "string", // e.g., "Asia"
  "hobbies": ["string"], // e.g., ["music", "cooking"]
  "languages": ["string"], // e.g., ["English", "Mandarin"]
  "bio": "string", // Max 200 characters
  "createdAt": "timestamp"
}

docs.title: Match Records
docs.text:
Tracks user pairings.

  • Collection: matches
  • Document: <matchId>
  • Fields: 
    {
  "user1Id": "string",
  "user2Id": "string",
  "createdAt": "timestamp",
  "oneTime": boolean
}

docs.title: Message Storage
docs.text:
Stores messages with delivery delays.

  • Collection: messages
  • Document: <messageId>
  • Fields: 
    {
  "matchId": "string",
  "senderId": "string",
  "content": "string", // Max 1000 characters
  "emojis": ["string"],
  "queuedAt": "timestamp",
  "deliveryAt": "timestamp"
}

docs.title: Moderation Logs
docs.text:
Tracks reports and bans.

  • Collection: moderation
  • Document: <reportId>
  • Fields: 
    {
  "userId": "string", // Optional
  "messageId": "string", // Optional
  "reason": "string",
  "status": "string", // e.g., "pending", "resolved"
  "createdAt": "timestamp"
}

docs.title: 1. Entity Descriptions
docs.text:
Users Stores the core details of each pen pal, including personal info, language preferences, hobbies, and blocked users. This entity is the foundation for all matchmaking and messaging operations.

Matches Represents a pairing between two users for correspondence. Includes match metadata such as timestamps, status, and preferences.

Messages Stores the conversation between matched users. Each message references the sender, recipient, and time sent.

Reports Keeps track of user-reported issues such as harassment or inappropriate content, linking the reporting user, the reported user, and the context.

CulturalProfiles Holds optional cultural information about users (hobbies, cultural background, languages spoken) used to improve match recommendations.

docs.title: Users Collection
docs.text: Field Type Constraints Description uid string Primary Key, Unique Unique identifier for each user displayName string Optional User’s display name email string Required, Unique User’s email for login languages array of strings Optional Languages the user speaks hobbies array of strings Optional User interests blockedUsers array of strings Optional List of users blocked by this user createdAt timestamp Default: now Account creation time

docs.title: Matches Collection
docs.text: Field Type Constraints Description matchId string Primary Key Unique ID for each match user1Id string Required UID of first user user2Id string Required UID of second user status string Optional e.g., active, completed matchedAt timestamp Default: now Time match was created

docs.title: Messages Collection
docs.text: Field Type Constraints Description messageId string Primary Key Unique ID for each message matchId string Required Reference to the match senderId string Required UID of sender recipientId string Required UID of recipient text string Required Message content sentAt timestamp Default: now Time message was sent

docs.title: Reports Collection
docs.text: Field Type Constraints Description reportId string Primary Key Unique ID for the report reportingUserId string Required UID of reporting user reportedUserId string Required UID of reported user reason string Required Description of issue createdAt timestamp Default: now Time report was filed

docs.title: CulturalProfiles Collection
docs.text: Field Type Constraints Description profileId string Primary Key Unique ID for the cultural profile userId string Required UID of the user languages array of strings Optional Languages spoken hobbies array of strings Optional Hobbies and interests culturalNotes string Optional Any additional cultural info

docs.title: 3. Relationships & Cardinalities
docs.text:
• Users and Matches: One User can participate in many Matches. Each Match connects exactly two Users. (One-to-Many)
  • Matches and Messages: One Match can have many Messages. Each Message belongs to exactly one Match. (One-to-Many)
  • Users and Reports: One User can file multiple Reports. Each Report references one reporting user and one reported user. (One-to-Many)
  • Users and CulturalProfiles: One User can have one optional CulturalProfile. (One-to-One)

docs.title: 4. Indexes & Keys
docs.text:
• uid serves as the unique identifier for Users.
  • matchId, messageId, reportId, profileId serve as document IDs for other collections.
  • Composite indexes may be added for queries such as:
  • Retrieve all matches for a user (user1Id or user2Id)
  • Retrieve messages for a match (matchId + sentAt)

docs.title: 5. Deployment Information
docs.text:
• The database is deployed on Firebase Firestore, a NoSQL, document-based database.
  • Collections are created dynamically when data is added.
  • Backend access is secured via Firebase Admin SDK and service account credentials.
  • Real-time updates allow chat messages and matches to sync instantly between users.

docs.title: 6. Choice Justification
docs.text:
• Firestore Advantages for this Project:
  • Real-time syncing – essential for messaging functionality.
  • Flexible schema – allows optional fields like hobbies and cultural notes without strict table constraints.
  • Seamless integration – works smoothly with Firebase Authentication and Cloud Functions.
  • Scalability – handles growing number of users and matches efficiently.

docs.title: Features
docs.text: GlobeTalk offers a rich set of features to foster cultural exchange and global connections through text-based messaging.

docs.title: Random Matchmaking
docs.text:
• Connect with a random pen pal from another country based on time zone or language preferences.
  • Choose between one-time messages or ongoing correspondence.
  • Example: Select "Spanish" as a preferred language to match with a pen pal from Spain or Latin America.

docs.title: Asynchronous Messaging
docs.text:
• Send and receive text-based letters with a 12-hour delivery delay to mimic postal mail.
  • Messages support basic emojis for expressive communication.
  • Messages are stored privately and accessible only to matched users.

docs.title: Cultural Profiles
docs.text:
• Create a short intro about yourself (e.g., age range, hobbies, region).
  • View anonymous facts about your pen pal, such as regional holidays or sayings.
  • Example: Learn that your pen pal from Japan celebrates Obon, a festival honoring ancestors.

docs.title: Safety & Moderation
docs.text:
• Anonymous chats with no personal identifiers (names, emails).
  • Flag inappropriate content or block users for a safe experience.
  • Text-only messaging (no media or file sharing) to reduce risks.

docs.text:

    git clone https://github.com/example/globetalk.git
cd globetalk

    npm init -y

  3. Install Dependencies 

    npm install eslint --save-dev

  5. Install Firebase CLI: 
    npm install -g firebase-tools

    firebase login

    firebase init

  8. Select Firestore, Functions, and Hosting, then follow the prompts.

  9. Run Locally

  10. Start the development server: 
    firebase emulators:start
  11. Open http://localhost:5000 in your browser.

docs.title: 1. Why use Notion
docs.text: Our group uses Notion because it gives us a single, flexible workspace where we can organise everything related to the project. Instead of juggling multiple apps for notes, documents, and task lists, Notion lets us keep all of that in one place. This makes it easy for everyone to find the latest version of meeting notes, project requirements, or deadlines without digging through endless chats or emails. Notion also helps us stay on the same page about responsibilities. With shared task boards and checklists, we can see who is working on what and track progress together. The fact that it’s cloud-based means any update, whether someone adds a new task, edits a document, or checks off a task is instantly visible to the whole group. Another big reason we like Notion is how simple it is to customise. We’ve been able to set up pages that actually fit how we work, from a central project dashboard down to quick task lists. This flexibility makes it feel more like our workspace rather than just another generic tool. In short, Notion helps us stay organised, reduce confusion, and work more smoothly as a team without wasting time searching for scattered information.

docs.title: 2. Pros of using Notion as a Project Management Tool
docs.text: • Cost-effective – As an all in one platform, Notion reduces the need to invest in separate tools for CRM, onboarding, and project management. • Easy to use – Once you get familiar with its features, creating pages and managing content becomes simpler compared to many other platforms. • Efficient – With built-in templates, shortcuts, and powerful features for note taking, task assignment, and workflow automation, Notion helps teams save time. Since everything can be done within one workspace, there’s no need to constantly switch between apps. • Accessible anywhere – Notion works seamlessly across devices, whether on web, desktop, or mobile, making it easy for users to stay connected and productive from any location.

docs.title: Colour Scheme
docs.text: We selected a blue colour scheme for our GlobeTalk interface. Blue is mostly associated with the sky and the ocean, which highlights the theme of global connection and being able to interact with people around the world and not be limited by geographical borders. We chose a lighter shade of blue for most of the pages’ background to incorporate a sense of calmness, while using the app, and a darker blue for the buttons to provide a contrast to guide user focus to key actions.

docs.title: Images and  Icons
docs.text:
• Globe Icon: The globe icon is to show that platform is international and allows user to connect at a global level.
  • Clouds: The clouds symbolize openness and the idea of being connected “through the air”, similar to how messages travel digitally across the world.
  • Human illustrations: The human illustrations portray the diversity in race, gender, cultures and interests of people who could potentially use our platform.

docs.title: Alignment with GlobeTalk’s Values
docs.text:
GlobeTalk’s purpose is to help users find like-minded friends worldwide through language and cultural exchange. Our values are Global Diversity, Anonymity and Safety, Meaningful Connection, Respect and Kindness. The blue tones, global imagery, and soft illustrations work together to reinforce these values by:

  • Conveying the global connectivity of the platform.
  • Promoting feelings of safety and trust for international communication.
  • Creating an inviting and visually engaging space that encourages exploration.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
This project follows the Scrum methodology, an Agile framework for managing and completing complex software development projects. Scrum is particularly well-suited to our Virtual Pen Pals website because it emphasizes:

  • Short, iterative development cycles (sprints)
  • Frequent reviews
  • Adaptability to change

This ensures that our group delivers a functional and high-quality product within the set deadlines.

docs.title: 2. Why Scrum is Suitable for Our Project
docs.text:
Our development cycle consists of four sprints spread across approximately three months, each focusing on specific deliverables. Scrum allows our group to:

  • Break the project into manageable parts – making it easier to meet deadlines.
  • Receive and apply feedback early – enabling course corrections without major rework.
  • Maintain clear team roles and responsibilities – ensuring accountability.
  • Track progress visually – using tools like Scrum boards or digital equivalents.

Given that our sprints vary in length, Scrum’s flexibility ensures we can still deliver working features at the end of each sprint, regardless of duration.

docs.title: 3. Scrum Roles in Our Team
docs.text:
• Product Owner (PO) – Responsible for defining the product vision, prioritizing features, and ensuring the project meets user needs. Our Product Owner: Shaneel Kassen

  • Scrum Master – Facilitates Scrum events, removes obstacles, and ensures the team follows Scrum principles. Our Scrum Master: Paballo Lipopo

  • Development Team – Responsible for designing, coding, testing, and integrating all project features. Our Development Team:

  • Nfundwenhle Ezra Nkontwana
  • Kuhlula Mambane
  • Tiyani Mabunda
  • Bongani Nobela
  • Paballo Lipopo

docs.title: 4. Scrum Events Used in the Project
docs.text:
1. Sprint Planning – At the start of each sprint, the team selects the features and tasks to be completed, based on priority.

  2. Daily Stand-ups – Short daily meetings to discuss:

  3. What was done yesterday
  4. What will be done today

  5. Any obstacles faced

  6. Sprint Review – At the end of each sprint, the team demonstrates the new features to stakeholders for feedback.

  7. Sprint Retrospective – After each review, the team evaluates what worked well and what can be improved in the next sprint.

docs.title: 5. Conclusion
docs.text:
By applying the Scrum methodology, our group can:

  • Efficiently manage development tasks
  • Respond quickly to feedback
  • Ensure consistent progress throughout the project

The time-boxed nature of sprints and the focus on delivering usable increments will help us meet the final deadline while ensuring a high-quality Virtual Pen Pals website.

docs.title: Frontend: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript with Figma for UI Design
docs.text: For the frontend of GlobeTalk we use core web technologies HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to build an accessible and lightweight user interface. This allows us to rapidly prototype key views such as the matchmaking screen, cultural profiles, and chat interface without the overhead of frameworks. By converting designs made in Figma directly into code our team ensures that the chat page, profile views, and cultural explorer match the intended UI/UX design. Since the project emphasizes simplicity, accessibility, and cross-browser compatibility, sticking with raw web technologies aligns well with our goals. Backend: Node.js with Express + Firebase The backend logic for GlobeTalk is handled using a hybrid approach: - Node.js with Express hosts custom APIs (e.g., Moderation API) deployed on Render. These handle tasks like reporting users, blocking/unblocking, and moderation logs. - Firebase Cloud Functions are used for other serverless tasks, such as simulating message delivery delays (to mimic postal mail). This setup gives us both control (for our custom APIs) and scalability (through Firebase’s serverless infrastructure). Database: Firebase Firestore GlobeTalk stores its core data in Firebase Firestore, which supports the project’s dynamic and semi-structured needs: - User Profiles (region, language, hobbies, cultural facts). - Match Records (pairings between pen pals with timestamps). - Messages (stored with delays, sender/receiver IDs, and text content). - Moderation Logs (reports, blocks, flags). Firestore’s real-time syncing also allows chat updates and profile data to be retrieved instantly, which is essential for asynchronous messaging and user interaction.

docs.title: Hosting: Render + GitHub Pages
docs.text:
• The APIs (e.g., Moderation API, future Messaging API) are deployed on Render, which provides free hosting with environment variable support for Firebase keys.
  • The frontend is hosted via GitHub Pages, making the static HTML/CSS/JS easily accessible for end-users and simple to redeploy during development. This hybrid setup keeps deployment costs low while giving us flexibility and scalability.

docs.title: Authentication and Security: Firebase Authentication
docs.text: User accounts are managed with Firebase Authentication, which enables anonymous matching while protecting real user data. Users never share personal details (names or emails) instead, unique identifiers are generated. Firebase Auth also integrates directly with Firestore, so security rules can enforce that users only access their own profiles and message threads.

docs.title: DevOps & CI/CD: GitHub Actions with Render Deployment
docs.text: For CI/CD, we use GitHub Actions to automate builds and deployments: - Every push to the main branch triggers builds and redeployment to Render for backend APIs. - GitHub Pages auto-deploys frontend changes directly from the repository. This ensures that team members can work collaboratively, and new features are pushed live without manual intervention.

docs.title: Testing: Postman, Jest, and User Feedback
docs.text:
• Postman is used to test API endpoints (/report, /block, /unblock, /listBlocked).
  • Jest is considered for frontend unit tests (e.g., input validation, emoji picker logic).
  • Google Forms User Feedback complements technical testing, providing real-world usability insights. This combination ensures both technical correctness and positive user experience, which is critical for GlobeTalk.

docs.text: GlobeTalk's user interface is built with HTML, CSS, and Vanilla JavaScript, designed for simplicity and responsiveness.

docs.title: UI/UX DESIGN EXPLANATION FOR OUR WEBSITE
Introduction
docs.text: The UI/UX design for GlobeTalk focuses on simplicity, accessibility, and a visually engaging experience to facilitate global connections between users through pen pal interactions. The design prioritizes clarity, user guidance, and real-time interactivity, ensuring that users of varying technical skills can navigate the platform with ease.

docs.title: Design Philosophy
docs.text:
The GlobeTalk interface emphasizes: - Clean, modern aesthetics: A blue gradient header provides a welcoming and calm visual, reflecting trustworthiness and global connectivity. - Card-based layouts: User profiles, pen pal suggestions, and active pen pal lists are presented in cards, balancing readability with visual appeal. - Mobile-first, responsive design: All pages are designed to function seamlessly across desktop and mobile devices.

Benefit: Users can intuitively explore profiles and features without cognitive overload, making it easy to engage with the platform.

docs.title: Navigation Bar:
docs.text:
• Located at the top of each page, featuring links to Home, Find Pen Pal, Chats, My Penpals, and Settings & Safety.
  • The Logout button is placed on the top-right for quick access.
  • Consistent placement across pages ensures users can navigate intuitively.

docs.title: Dashboard Layout (Home Page):
docs.text:
• User Card: Displays the logged-in user’s profile with username, timezone, and a short bio.
  • Pen Pal Suggestions: Each suggested pen pal is presented as a card with region, hobbies, and languages.
  • Active Pen Pals List: Scrollable card layout showing all active connections, making it easy to view and access conversations.

Benefit: Users can quickly identify personal information, find new pen pals, and manage existing connections from a single dashboard.

docs.title: Purpose:
docs.text: Allows users to set preferences to find compatible pen pals.

docs.title: Form-Based User Input:
docs.text:
• Language Preference: Dropdown menu for selecting communication language.
  • Region/Timezone: Dropdown for selecting compatible time zones.
  • Find My Pen Pal Button: Submits preferences and generates suggested matches.

docs.title: Guidance & Accessibility:
docs.text:
Clear placeholder text and sub-label instructions help users understand required input.

Benefit: The form simplifies matching with like-minded users across the globe, making the experience intuitive and efficient.

docs.title: Interface Elements:
docs.text:
• Cards: Used throughout the platform to display users, suggestions, and active pen pals.
  • Include profile avatar, username, region/timezone, hobbies, and languages.
  • Structured hierarchically to emphasize the most relevant information first.
  • Buttons:
  • Styled with a gradient and hover effects to highlight interactivity.
  • Clearly labelled actions, such as Find My Pen Pal, enhance usability.

docs.title: Accessibility and Usability
docs.text:
• Colour Contrast: Blue and white gradients ensure readability for users with visual impairments.
  • Typography: Bold, sans-serif fonts are used for clarity.
  • Responsive Design: Layout adapts to various screen sizes, ensuring functional and visual consistency across devices.

Benefit: The design ensures users from different regions and technical backgrounds can comfortably use the platform.

docs.title: Chats Page Interface
docs.text:
The Chats page adopts a split view layout that balances functionality and simplicity:

  • Left Panel Conversation List: Vertically scrollable list of active chats, with the selected chat highlighted.
  • Right Panel Chat Window: Clean message interface with distinguishable chat bubbles.
  • Outgoing messages use a vibrant gradient tone.
  • Incoming messages remain neutral for contrast.
  • Top Action Bar: Includes the recipient’s username and a Block button for safety.
  • Message Input Area: Includes emoji icon and Send button styled in purple.

Benefit: The two-column structure allows users to manage multiple conversations efficiently, mirroring modern messaging experiences.

docs.title: Penpals Page Interface
docs.text:
Focuses on managing user connections through search and request tools.

  • Search Section: At the top, users can search by username using a labelled input field and purple “Search” button.
  • Your Penpals Card: Displays current pen pals; when empty, a friendly prompt encourages users to connect.
  • Requests Section:
  • Requests To You: Cards showing requester’s username with Accept / Decline buttons.
  • Requests You Sent: Displays pending outgoing requests.

The gradient blue background provides visual separation, while white cards maintain contrast and readability.

Benefit: Users get a clear overview of their social interactions in one place.

docs.title: User Feedback and Accessibility
docs.text:
Across all pages: - Responsive layouts for all devices - Buttons and inputs provide hover/focus feedback - Error messages and confirmations appear in context

Benefit: Ensures an inclusive and straightforward experience that supports global friendships through intuitive communication.

docs.title: Profile Customization Interface
docs.text: The Profile Page allows users to define personal characteristics and interests.

docs.title: Layout and Design Elements:
docs.text:
• Form Based Structure: Vertically oriented form with clear labels (Age Range, Gender, Interests, Short Bio).
  • Dropdown Menus: Used for Age Range and Gender for consistency.
  • Text Fields: Allow flexible self-expression.
  • Primary Action Button: “Save Change” button uses purple gradient and is clearly visible.

docs.title: User Experience Considerations:
docs.text:
• Simplicity and guidance through placeholder text
  • Visual confirmation after saving
  • Consistent spacing, rounded elements, and typography

Benefit: Promotes quick setup with easy personalization.

docs.title: Settings and Safety Interface
docs.text: Allows users to manage key preferences and access safety information.

docs.title: Layout and Navigation:
docs.text:
• Two-Section Layout:
  • Policy Access Cards
  • Profile Information
  • Policy Cards: Privacy Policy and Terms of Service displayed as interactive cards.
  • Profile Information Section: Dropdowns for Language and Region/Time Zone.

docs.title: Visual Design:
docs.text:
• Clean sans-serif typography
  • Blue-to-teal gradients for trust and calmness
  • Light borders, rounded corners for clarity and touch-friendliness

docs.title: Overall UX Integration
docs.text:
GlobeTalk’s UX is guided by principles of: - Consistency - Clarity - Accessibility - Feedback - User control

A unified visual language (gradient colors, card layouts, structured spacing) reduces cognitive load. Real-time interaction responses boost confidence. Responsive layouts ensure functionality across devices.

Users maintain full control over connections, preferences, and personal data—empowering comfortable global communication in an inclusive, user-centered environment.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: Learn how to use GlobeTalk as a user or developer.

docs.title: For Users
docs.text:
1. Sign Up
  2. Create an account using Firebase Authentication (Google).

  3. Set up your profile with region, hobbies, and languages.

  4. Find a Pen Pal

  5. Go to the Match Screen and select preferences (e.g., language: Spanish, time zone: UTC-3).
  6. Choose one-time or ongoing correspondence.

  7. Example: Match with a user from Argentina for ongoing chats.

  8. Send a Message

  9. In the Compose Letter section, write a message (e.g., "Hello! What's your favorite holiday? 😊").

  10. Submit to queue it for delivery in 12 hours.

  11. Explore Cultural Facts

  12. Visit the Cultural Explorer to view facts about your pen pal’s region.

  13. Example: Learn about Diwali if matched with an Indian user.

  14. Stay Safe

  15. Use the Settings & Safety section to block or report users.
  16. Example: Report a message for inappropriate content.

docs.title: For Developers
docs.text:
1. API Integration
  2. Authenticate with Firebase to get a token.
  3. Use the Matchmaking API to connect users.

  4. Example: Send a POST /match request to pair a user with a Spanish-speaking pen pal.

  5. Local Testing

  6. Run Firebase emulators to test API endpoints locally.

  7. Use Postman to send requests to http://localhost:5001/globetalk/us-central1/api.

  8. Database Access

  9. Query the users collection to retrieve profiles.
  10. Example: Fetch a pen pal’s profile with GET /profile/<userId>.

docs.title: Example Workflow
docs.text:
1. Sign up and set your profile to "Region: Europe, Language: French."
  2. Match with a pen pal from France.
  3. Send a message: "Bonjour! Tell me about French culture! 🇫🇷"
  4. After 12 hours, receive a reply and view their cultural fact about Bastille Day.

docs.title: API Overview
docs.text: GlobeTalk provides a set of RESTful APIs to manage matchmaking, messaging, user profiles, and moderation. These APIs are built with Firebase Functions and integrate with Firebase Firestore for data storage.

docs.title: API Modules
docs.text:
• Matchmaking API: Connect users with available pen pals based on filters like language or time zone.
  • Message API: Handle sending, delaying, and retrieving text-based messages.
  • Profile API: Manage user cultural profiles, including region and hobbies.
  • Moderation API: Report users, manage bans, and review flagged content.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: All APIs require Firebase Authentication tokens. Include the token in the Authorization header as Bearer <token>.

docs.title: Base URL
docs.text: https://us-central1-globetalk.cloudfunctions.net/api

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
1. Set up Firebase Authentication for your app.
  2. Obtain an access token for authenticated requests.
  3. Use the endpoints below to interact with GlobeTalk's features.

docs.title: Matchmaking API
docs.text: The Matchmaking API connects users with random pen pals based on filters like language or time zone.

docs.title: POST /match
docs.text: Matches the authenticated user with a new pen pal.

docs.title: Request
docs.text:
• Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>
  • Body: 
    {
  "language": "string", // Optional: e.g., "Spanish"
  "timezone": "string", // Optional: e.g., "UTC+1"
  "oneTime": boolean // true for one-time message, false for ongoing
}

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
• Status: 200 OK
  • Body: 
    {
  "matchId": "string",
  "penPal": {
    "userId": "string",
    "region": "string",
    "language": "string"
  }
}

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
curl -X POST https://us-central1-globetalk.cloudfunctions.net/api/match \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"language": "Spanish", "oneTime": false}'

docs.title: Message API
docs.text: The Message API handles sending, delaying, and retrieving text-based messages between matched users.

docs.title: POST /messages
docs.text: Sends a new message with a 12-hour delivery delay.

docs.title: Request
docs.text:
• Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>
  • Body: 
    {
  "matchId": "string",
  "content": "string", // Text message, max 1000 characters
  "emojis": ["string"] // Optional: Array of emoji codes
}

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
• Status: 201 Created
  • Body: 
    {
  "messageId": "string",
  "status": "queued",
  "deliveryTime": "ISO8601 timestamp"
}

docs.title: GET /messages/{matchId}
docs.text: Retrieves all messages for a match.

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
• Status: 200 OK
  • Body: 
    [
  {
    "messageId": "string",
    "content": "string",
    "senderId": "string",
    "timestamp": "ISO8601 timestamp"
  }
]

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
curl -X POST https://us-central1-globetalk.cloudfunctions.net/api/messages \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"matchId": "abc123", "content": "Hello from Brazil! 😊"}'

docs.title: Moderation API
docs.text: The Moderation API handles reporting users, managing bans, and reviewing flagged content.

docs.title: POST /report
docs.text: Reports a message or user for inappropriate content.

docs.title: Request
docs.text:
• Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>
  • Body: 
    {
  "messageId": "string", // Optional
  "userId": "string", // Optional
  "reason": "string" // e.g., "Inappropriate language"
}

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
• Status: 201 Created
  • Body: 
    {
  "reportId": "string",
  "status": "submitted"
}

docs.title: POST /block
docs.text: Blocks a user to prevent further communication.

docs.title: Request
docs.text:
• Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>
  • Body: 
    {
  "userId": "string"
}

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
• Status: 200 OK
  • Body: 
    {
  "blocked": true
}

docs.title: Profile API
docs.text: The Profile API manages user cultural profiles, including region, hobbies, and languages.

docs.title: PUT /profile
docs.text: Updates the authenticated user's profile.

docs.title: Request
docs.text:
• Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>
  • Body: 
    {
  "region": "string", // e.g., "South America"
  "hobbies": ["string"], // e.g., ["reading", "travel"]
  "languages": ["string"], // e.g., ["English", "Portuguese"]
  "bio": "string" // Max 200 characters
}

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
• Status: 200 OK
  • Body: 
    {
  "userId": "string",
  "updated": true
}

docs.title: GET /profile/{userId}
docs.text: Retrieves a pen pal's anonymous profile.

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
• Status: 200 OK
  • Body: 
    {
  "region": "string",
  "hobbies": ["string"],
  "languages": ["string"],
  "bio": "string",
  "funFact": "string" // e.g., "Celebrates Diwali"
}

docs.title: Chatflow sequence
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant UA as User A
    participant System as System
    participant DB as Firestore
    participant Trans as Translation API
    participant FCM as Firebase Cloud Messaging
    participant UB as User B

    UA->>System: Send message to User B
    System->>DB: Store original message
    System->>Trans: Request translation (if needed)
    Trans-->>System: Return translated message
    System->>DB: Store translated message
    System->>FCM: Send push notification
    FCM-->>UB: Deliver notification
    System-->>UA: Confirm message sent
    System-->>UB: Real-time message update
    UB->>System: Send reaction/emoji
    System->>DB: Store reaction
    System-->>UA: Real-time reaction update
    Note right of System: All messages stored with timestamp
    Note left of UB: User receives both original and translated text

docs.title: Admin Moderation sequence
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant User as Reporting User
    participant System as System
    participant ContentAPI as Content Moderation API
    participant Admin as Administrator
    participant DB as Firestore
    participant Target as Reported User
    User->>System: Report inappropriate content
    System->>DB: Store report with metadata
    System->>ContentAPI: Analyze flagged content
    ContentAPI-->>System: Return moderation score
    alt Auto-moderate (high confidence)
        System->>DB: Auto-delete offensive content
        System->>DB: Log moderation action
        System-->>User: Notify action taken
    else Requires human review
        System->>Admin: Flag for manual review
        Admin->>System: Access Admin Dashboard
        System->>DB: Fetch report details
        DB-->>Admin: Display report and content
        Admin->>System: Make moderation decision
        alt Ban user
            System->>DB: Update user status to banned
            System->>Target: Send account suspension notice
        else Warn user
            System->>Target: Send warning notification
            System->>DB: Log warning
        else Dismiss report
            System->>DB: Mark report as dismissed
        end
        System->>DB: Update report status
        System-->>User: Notify resolution
        System->>DB: Log admin action
    end
    Note over System: All actions logged for audit trail
    Note over Admin: Admin can generate reports for analytics

docs.title: Friendship System Sequence
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant UA as User A
    participant System as System
    participant MatchAPI as Matchmaking API
    participant FriendAPI as Friendship API
    participant DB as Firestore
    participant FCM as Push Notifications
    participant UB as User B

    UA->>System: Access contact search
    System->>MatchAPI: Request user suggestions
    MatchAPI->>DB: Query compatible users
    DB-->>MatchAPI: Return filtered users
    MatchAPI-->>System: Provide suggestions
    System-->>UA: Display potential contacts

    UA->>System: Send friend request to User B
    System->>FriendAPI: Process friend request
    FriendAPI->>DB: Check existing relationship

    alt No existing relationship
        FriendAPI->>DB: Create friendship record (pending)
        DB-->>FriendAPI: Confirm creation
        FriendAPI->>FCM: Send notification to User B
        FCM-->>UB: Friend request notification
        FriendAPI-->>System: Request sent confirmation
        System-->>UA: Show request pending

        UB->>System: View friend requests
        System->>DB: Fetch pending requests
        DB-->>System: Return requests list
        System-->>UB: Display friend requests

        UB->>System: Accept friend request
        System->>FriendAPI: Process acceptance
        FriendAPI->>DB: Update friendship status to accepted
        FriendAPI->>FCM: Notify User A of acceptance
        FCM-->>UA: Friend request accepted notification
        FriendAPI-->>System: Friendship established
        System-->>UB: Show new contact in list

        Note over System: Both users can now chat

    else Relationship exists
        FriendAPI-->>System: Return existing status
        System-->>UA: Show current relationship status
    end

    Note over DB: Mutual friendship enforced by Cloud Functions
    Note over System: All friendship changes trigger real-time updates

docs.title: User State Diagram
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Guest: User visits app

    Guest --> Registering: Click Sign Up
    Guest --> LoggingIn: Click Sign In

    Registering --> Onboarding: Registration successful
    LoggingIn --> Onboarding: First time login
    LoggingIn --> Active: Returning user login

    Onboarding --> ProfileSetup: Begin profile creation
    ProfileSetup --> Active: Profile completed

    state Active {
        [*] --> Online
        Online --> Browsing: Browse contacts
        Online --> Chatting: Open chat
        Online --> Managing: Access settings

        Browsing --> Online: Return to home
        Browsing --> RequestSent: Send friend request

        RequestSent --> Online: Request processed
        RequestSent --> Connected: Request accepted

        Connected --> Chatting: Start conversation

        Chatting --> Online: Close chat
        Chatting --> Typing: Composing message
        Chatting --> Reacting: Add emoji reaction

        Typing --> Chatting: Send message
        Reacting --> Chatting: Reaction added

        Managing --> Online: Settings saved
        Managing --> ProfileEditing: Edit profile
        Managing --> PrivacySettings: Adjust privacy

        ProfileEditing --> Managing: Profile updated
        PrivacySettings --> Managing: Privacy updated

        Online --> Idle: No activity (5 min)
        Idle --> Online: User interaction
        Idle --> Offline: Extended inactivity
        Offline --> Online: User returns
    }

    Active --> Reported: User gets reported
    Active --> Blocked: User blocks someone
    Active --> Suspended: Admin action
    Active --> Deactivated: User deactivates
    Active --> Deleted: User deletes account

    Reported --> UnderReview: Admin reviews report
    UnderReview --> Active: Report dismissed
    UnderReview --> Warned: Warning issued
    UnderReview --> Suspended: Violation confirmed

    Warned --> Active: Warning acknowledged

    Suspended --> Active: Suspension lifted
    Suspended --> Banned: Repeated violations

    Blocked --> Active: User can unblock

    Deactivated --> Active: User reactivates
    Deactivated --> Deleted: Auto-delete after 30 days

    Banned --> [*]: Account permanently closed
    Deleted --> [*]: Account permanently removed

    note right of Active
        User can perform all app functions:
        - Send/receive messages
        - Make friend requests
        - Update profile
        - Access all features
    end note

    note right of Suspended
        Limited access:
        - Cannot send messages
        - Cannot make friend requests
        - Read-only access
    end note

    note right of Banned
        No access:
        - Account locked
        - Cannot log in
        - All data preserved for audit
    end note

docs.title: Chat State Diagram
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> NoConversation: User has no active chats

    NoConversation --> SearchingContacts: User searches for contacts
    NoConversation --> ViewingRequests: User checks friend requests

    SearchingContacts --> RequestSent: Send friend request
    SearchingContacts --> NoConversation: Cancel search

    ViewingRequests --> RequestAccepted: Accept friend request
    ViewingRequests --> RequestRejected: Reject friend request
    ViewingRequests --> NoConversation: Close requests

    RequestSent --> Pending: Waiting for response
    RequestAccepted --> Connected: Friendship established
    RequestRejected --> NoConversation: Request declined

    Pending --> Connected: Request accepted by other user
    Pending --> RequestRejected: Request declined by other user
    Pending --> NoConversation: Cancel pending request

    Connected --> ChatActive: Open chat window

    state ChatActive {
        [*] --> Viewing

        Viewing --> Composing: Start typing message
        Viewing --> Reacting: Click emoji reaction
        Viewing --> MenuOpen: Open chat menu

        Composing --> Sending: Send message
        Composing --> Viewing: Cancel message

        Sending --> MessageSent: Message delivered
        MessageSent --> Viewing: Return to chat

        Reacting --> ReactionSent: Reaction added
        ReactionSent --> Viewing: Return to chat

        MenuOpen --> Viewing: Close menu
        MenuOpen --> Blocking: Block user
        MenuOpen --> Reporting: Report user
        MenuOpen --> ViewingProfile: View user profile

        ViewingProfile --> Viewing: Return to chat

        Blocking --> [*]: Chat blocked, exit to home
        Reporting --> [*]: Report submitted, exit to home
    }

    ChatActive --> Connected: Close chat window
    ChatActive --> Blocked: User blocked
    ChatActive --> Reported: User reported

    Connected --> Unfriended: Remove friend
    Unfriended --> NoConversation: Friendship ended

    Blocked --> [*]: Chat permanently closed
    Reported --> UnderReview: Report submitted for moderation

    UnderReview --> Connected: Report dismissed
    UnderReview --> Blocked: Report confirmed

    %% Message status substates
    state MessageSent {
        Delivered --> Read: Recipient opens chat
        Delivered --> Translated: Auto-translation applied
        Translated --> Read: Recipient reads translated message
    }

    note right of Connected
        Users can exchange messages,
        see online status,
        react with emojis
    end note

    note right of Blocked
        No further communication possible,
        chat history preserved
    end note

    note left of Pending
        Friend request sent,
        waiting for other user's response
    end note
